probe.summary: A probe run asks Plex cheap aggregate questions (COUNT and MAX/SUM per extracted table), and fingerprints the answers together with the report's YAML and view SQL. If the fingerprint equals the last clean run's, extraction and view creation are skipped; otherwise the full pipeline runs. It exists because every pipeline is a full WRITE_TRUNCATE refresh (99 full table pulls), so four prod runs a day need a cheap change check. Label Design pioneered it on 2026-10-01. Measured on Plex test: 82 probe queries took 12.4 s in total.
steps: The dispatcher or a scheduler starts the Cloud Run job; RUN_MODE is probe, full, scheduled or retry.
main() loads the YAML from GCS and opens the Plex ODBC connection.
probe_kind returns auto (probe_mode: auto), explicit (a probe.queries block, Label Design) or none.
may_skip is true for RUN_MODE=probe, and for an explicit probe on a scheduled run; false for full, retry, and scheduled auto-probe runs.
ensure_probe_log_table, then last_applied_probe reads the newest applied fingerprint and snapshot.
run_probe runs one aggregate per extraction and hashes the sorted snapshot plus the config and SQL hash (sha256, 32 chars).
If may_skip and the fingerprint is unchanged: log skipped, record dispatch outcome skipped, send the short 'Probe ran - nothing to update' email unless EMAIL_MODE=on_error.
Otherwise run every extraction and create or replace the views (a failed view is retried once).
After a clean run write probe_log applied; a partial or failed run writes failed and the reference does not advance.
record_dispatch_outcome writes the outcome onto the etl_dispatch_log row; the full email names the changed tables.
probe.change_detection: COUNT(*) catches added or removed rows. The extraction's probe: [...] list adds MAX(change date or key) columns (71 of 82 extractions have one) and sum:Col entries for SUM, which makes edits visible on views with no change date; SUM of key columns is refused (Plex 32-bit overflow) and Plex refuses SUM on bit columns. Columns were chosen by scripts/generate_probe_columns.py. YAML (_config_sha) and every view's SQL are in the fingerprint. Floats are rounded to 4 places. The YAML key is probe_mode, not probe:, because older images crash on a string probe:.
probe.failure_policy: No retries: prod max_retries is 0 and the prod -retry schedulers are gone. A failed, partial or lost run gets ONE follow-up probe from the dispatcher 15 minutes later (not if older than 6 hours; never a follow-up of a follow-up; a busy follow-up is not retried; a dispatch-failed start gets none). A failed run does not advance the fingerprint, so the follow-up re-runs in full. The probe fails open: a query error, bad column, empty aggregate or unreadable probe_log runs the full extraction and logs an inconclusive row.
gotchas: A quiet probe skips view creation, so a SQL-only deploy used to wait for Plex to change (OPEN_ITEMS L10). Since 2026-10-19 YAML and SQL are in the fingerprint; L10 stays open until the next SQL-only deploy proves it (the quiet run must log applied).
Code and image changes are not in the fingerprint; a quiet pipeline picks them up at the next changed probe, the 4 AM full run, or a hand start.
An edit on a table with no change date and no sum: column is invisible to the probe; the 4 AM full run bounds it at one day.
A permanently broken probe is invisible: query probe_log WHERE outcome='inconclusive'.
Busy tables (Part_v_Production, Part_v_Container) mean Work Orders and inventory usually run in full at 1 PM and 6 PM; that is correct.
A short email does not mean views were rebuilt, and job exit 0 does not mean the view exists; query it.
The first run after a fingerprint format change always runs in full.
probe.prod_vs_test: Only prod uses the probe to skip work. The dispatcher starts prod jobs with RUN_MODE=probe at 1 PM, 6 PM and 11 PM, and an unchanged fingerprint skips the run; the 4 AM run is RUN_MODE=full and never skips. Test jobs are started by Cloud Scheduler with no override, so RUN_MODE is scheduled: the probe still runs and its fingerprint is logged as the reference, but probe_may_skip returns false and the job extracts everything, every night. That keeps test a full nightly rehearsal of every query. The one exception is Label Design, whose explicit probe skips on scheduled runs in both environments.

steps: Work on your project's dev branch in its own worktree (ptbq-dev = dev, ptbq-scorecard = dev-scorecard, ptbq-sandbox = dev-sandbox, ptbq-label-design = dev-label-design); the primary folder C:\F\Parasol\plex-to-big-query is main, for merge and deploy only.
Commit with a CHANGELOG.md entry plus the matching docs/reports or reports-list update; change prod and test YAML together; stage by explicit path.
Open a PR into main and merge it (pushing a dev branch into main is blocked); make sure main is pushed so HEAD equals origin/main.

Config, SQL and infra: run ./scripts/deploy.sh from the primary folder. It runs deploy_preflight.sh, checks HEAD == origin/main, terraform plan -var-file=terraform.tfvars -out (tf_guard.py runs inside), prints plan_review.py (content changes vs line-ending noise, destroys flagged), asks you to type the change count, applies exactly that plan, then tags deploy/<UTC timestamp> and pushes it.

Python code ships as an image through Cloud Build: gcloud builds submit --config deploy/cloudbuild.yaml --project=voxdatalake --substitutions=SHORT_SHA=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD) . Steps: fetch-driver, build, push-sha, push-latest, deploy-all (every job in _ALL_JOBS, 30 jobs), smoke-test on the TEST job only. Terraform jobs ignore image changes.
Cloud Functions use gcloud functions deploy (commands in main.tf comments); Apps Script apps are pasted by hand. Prod schedule changes are SQL on PlexOps.etl_schedule.
Verify: terraform plan on clean main should list nothing; query the BigQuery view after a run; read PlexOps.etl_dispatch_log for prod.
guards: pre-commit: the folder must be on its own branch (override ALLOW_WRONG_FOLDER=1).
pre-commit: no non-merge commits on main (ALLOW_MAIN_COMMIT=1).
pre-commit: a dev branch carries only its own project's files and one commit may not mix projects (ALLOW_CROSS_PROJECT=1).
pre-commit: changes under reports/ or terraform/ (non-.md) need a staged CHANGELOG.md (ALLOW_NO_CHANGELOG=1).
pre-commit: prod and test YAML plex_view counts must match (ALLOW_YAML_MISMATCH=1).
pre-push: only local main goes to origin main, and no non-fast-forward push to main (ALLOW_MAIN_PUSH=1).
tf_guard.py runs on every terraform plan and apply and refuses unless: primary worktree, branch main, clean tree, HEAD == origin/main. TF_GUARD_OVERRIDE="reason" is for read-only plans only.
deploy.sh adds preflight, HEAD == origin/main, plan_review.py and a typed change count.
Never --no-verify; use an override only when the user explicitly wants the exception, and say so.

gotchas.title: Deployed to test does not mean prod is current
gotchas.detail: Prod drifted from main when gcloud storage cp updated one GCS path. The truth is terraform plan on clean pushed main; sync with ./scripts/deploy.sh, never a bare apply, never gcloud storage cp into prod reports/ or sql/.

gotchas.title: Two config files per pipeline
gotchas.detail: Prod and test YAML are separate; change both. Editing only prod made a test run log 22 extractions instead of 24 and exit 0 (2026-09-09). Check grep -c 'plex_view:'. In GCS the test files are under test/, in git under reports/test/.

gotchas.title: Exit 0 does not mean the view was created
gotchas.detail: A job can finish PARTIAL with exit 0. Query the view. Keep SAFE_CAST on both sides of every join.

gotchas.title: Apply from a dev branch rolls back other work
gotchas.detail: Happened 2026-09-23 (Label Design view). tf_guard.py now refuses; stop if plan_review.py lists a file you did not touch.

gotchas.title: Line endings faked plan changes
gotchas.detail: 8 of 30 changes were identical content on 2026-09-24; .gitattributes now pins LF.

gotchas.title: GitHub push 403
gotchas.detail: CLAUDE.md blames an org setting; auto-memory says the wrong gh account (emiliodparasol can push, emiliodom cannot). Check the active account first. Cause not fully confirmed.

gotchas.title: gcloud reauthentication wall
gotchas.detail: Org policy; only a human running gcloud auth login clears it. It blinded monitoring from midnight to 08:30 on 2026-10-20.

gotchas.title: Prod times live in a table
gotchas.detail: Change a time with SQL on PlexOps.etl_schedule; check etl_dispatch_log, not the scheduler list, to see if prod ran. Test jobs keep their nightly schedulers.

gotchas.title: Some schedule values are not in git
gotchas.detail: Sales Orders crons and retry cron and time zone come from the gitignored terraform.tfvars; variables.tf defaults are wrong. Live values come from docs only.

gotchas.title: Cloud Build traps
gotchas.detail: Every substitution must be used, bash variables need $$, SHORT_SHA must be passed on a manual submit, _ALL_JOBS must list every job.

gotchas.title: Names are immutable
gotchas.detail: Renaming a job or scheduler recreates it on var.image_url, which can be stale; check against a live job first.

gotchas.title: Goals tables and scope
gotchas.detail: Neither goals table is Terraform-managed; the resolver fails if one is missing; scope is an exact string match (Encapsulating vs Encapsulation gives a NULL goal).

gotchas.title: Sandbox rules
gotchas.detail: Built from a snapshot that expired after 2026-09-30; proposed_sql/ overrides are not deployed.

gotchas.title: Email subjects
gotchas.detail: [Plex ETL] - {Category}: {Pipeline} - {date}, shared by prod and test; up to 52 prod emails a day. Subject changes ship via Cloud Build.

gotchas.title: Stale rows on a 0-row Plex result
Deploy the dispatcher function first
gotchas.detail: etl-dispatcher is deployed with gcloud functions deploy before deploy.sh or the scheduler gets 404s.
